title: Alignment through Meta-Weighted Online Sampling: Bridging the Gap between Data Generation and Preference Optimization
claim: A meta-learner couples data generation and training to target online sampling, matching or beating baselines with far fewer generation and annotation calls.
layout: 2 panels: left a two-band pipeline (generation on top, training below) with a central meta-learner and circular arrows; right a combined line and bar chart across 3 iterations
description: The left panel has two tinted horizontal bands. The blue top band is labeled Generation. It flows left to right from an Offline Dataset icon, through an 'Adaptive Sample' arrow, to an LLM robot, then a 'Generate' arrow to a Responses chat bubble. The pink bottom band is labeled Training. It shows an offline dataset plus an online chat-bubble dataset, then a 'Weighted Train' arrow to an updated LLM robot. A brain-with-lightbulb Meta-Learner sits in the center, linked to both bands by curved orange and blue arrows that form a feedback loop. The right panel is a chart over Iter 1–3. Lines show AlpacaEval 2 win rate for Online DPO, SELM and MetaAPO, with MetaAPO highest and in purple. Hatched bars show generation and annotation ratio, and the MetaAPO bars are much shorter. Cartoon icons and pastel colors draw the eye first.
caption: Left: Overview of MetaAPO. MetaAPO employs a meta-learner to couple online data generation (top) and model training (bottom). The meta-learner adaptively assigns weights by evaluating offline data, guiding both targeted online sample generation and training on the weighted combination of offline and online samples. Right: Performance (left y-axis, line plots) and online generation and annotation ratio relative to Online DPO (right y-axis, bar plots) across training iterations for different methods.
abstract: Preference optimization is crucial for aligning large language models (LLMs) with human values and intentions. A significant challenge in this process is the distribution mismatch between pre-collected offline preference data and the evolving model policy. Existing methods attempt to reduce this gap using static heuristics or decoupled online sampling strategies, but they often fail to adapt to the model's dynamic learning state. To bridge this gap, we propose Meta-Weighted Adaptive Preference Optimization (MetaAPO), a novel framework that dynamically couples data generation with model training. MetaAPO employs a lightweight meta-learner, as an "alignment gap estimator", to evaluate the potential benefits of on-policy sampling in relation to offline data. This guides targeted online generation and assigns sample-wise meta-weights to the optimization objective, dynamically balancing the quality and distribution of online and offline data. Experiments on AlpacaEval 2, Arena-Hard and MT-Bench demonstrate that MetaAPO consistently outperforms existing preference optimization approaches across various settings, while reducing 42% in online annotation costs. Code is available at https://github.com/junming-yang/MetaAPO.
